classification.difficultyReason: Apply the supplied H-then-A-then-O labelling sequence to differently oriented triangles, using the marked right angle and theta; a completed example supplies the procedure.

inlines.text:
Label the sides of these right-angled triangles.
Remember that the hypotenuse is always opposite the right-angle.
Label ‘H’ first it is the longest side
Then label ‘O’, it is the last side left

spec.description: Permanent demonstration with boxed H, A and O labels. Numbered instructional arrows correspond to the three editable instructions below.
spec.mathematics: Right angle at the lower-left vertex; theta at the lower-right vertex. H is the diagonal, A the bottom side and O the vertical side.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied demonstration remains visible in Questions.

answer.short: H: diagonal; A: bottom side; O: left side.
answer.worked: The diagonal is opposite the right angle, so it is H. The bottom side meets $\theta$ and is not H, so it is A. The left side is opposite $\theta$, so it is O.
